attachments.landmark_a: anterior tubercle of atlas / basilar occiput

bands.name: Anterior longitudinal ligament

attachments.landmark_b: anterior vertebral bodies, continuing to sacrum

bands.mechanical_role: resists spinal extension; reinforces the anterior anulus fibrosus and anterior vertebral body/disc margins along the entire spine
bands.function_note: A single continuous band running the full length of the spine from atlas/occiput to sacrum, firmly attached to both vertebral bodies and intervertebral discs (unlike the PLL, which attaches mainly to discs).
bands.source: Bogduk N. Clinical and Radiological Anatomy of the Lumbar Spine, 5th ed. Churchill Livingstone/Elsevier, 2012 -- spinal ligament anatomy and biomechanical role.

function: The strongest and widest of the spinal longitudinal ligaments, resisting hyperextension along the entire vertebral column.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Bogduk N. Clinical and Radiological Anatomy of the Lumbar Spine, 5th ed. Churchill Livingstone/Elsevier, 2012 -- spinal ligament anatomy and biomechanical role.

attachments.landmark_a: basilar occiput / posterior C2 body (as the membrana tectoria continuation)

bands.name: Posterior longitudinal ligament

attachments.landmark_a: posterior vertebral bodies, within the vertebral canal
attachments.landmark_b: posterior vertebral bodies, continuing toward the sacrum

bands.mechanical_role: resists spinal flexion and posterior disc herniation; narrows markedly at the lumbar levels, correlating with the predominance of posterolateral (rather than pure posterior) disc herniations there
bands.function_note: Attaches mainly to the intervertebral discs and adjacent vertebral body margins rather than broadly across the vertebral body itself (unlike the ALL) -- and narrows substantially in the lumbar region, a structural fact commonly cited to help explain why lumbar disc herniations are typically posterolateral rather than directly posterior.
bands.source: Bogduk N. Clinical and Radiological Anatomy of the Lumbar Spine, 5th ed. Churchill Livingstone/Elsevier, 2012 -- spinal ligament anatomy and biomechanical role.

function: Lines the anterior wall of the vertebral canal, resisting flexion and providing a (regionally variable) barrier against posterior disc herniation.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Bogduk N. Clinical and Radiological Anatomy of the Lumbar Spine, 5th ed. Churchill Livingstone/Elsevier, 2012 -- spinal ligament anatomy and biomechanical role.

attachments.landmark_b: lamina, superior margin of vertebra below (repeating C2-sacrum)

bands.name: Ligamentum flavum

attachments.landmark_b: lamina, superior margin of vertebra below

bands.mechanical_role: connects adjacent laminae; its unusually high elastin content (~80%) lets it recoil after flexion and resist buckling into the canal during extension
bands.function_note: Unusual among ligaments for its high elastin-to-collagen ratio, giving it an inherent, prestressed elastic recoil that helps protect the spinal cord/cauda equina from buckling into the canal during extension -- and whose age-related hypertrophy/calcification is a well-documented contributor to lumbar spinal stenosis.
bands.source: Bogduk N. Clinical and Radiological Anatomy of the Lumbar Spine, 5th ed. Churchill Livingstone/Elsevier, 2012 -- spinal ligament anatomy and biomechanical role.

function: Connects the laminae of adjacent vertebrae from C2 to the sacrum, forming part of the posterior wall of the vertebral canal.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Bogduk N. Clinical and Radiological Anatomy of the Lumbar Spine, 5th ed. Churchill Livingstone/Elsevier, 2012 -- spinal ligament anatomy and biomechanical role.

bands.name: Interspinous ligament
bands.mechanical_role: resists excessive flexion; weakest of the segmental posterior ligaments, best developed in the lumbar region
bands.function_note: Thin and membranous in the cervical/thoracic regions but substantially thicker in the lumbar spine, where its posterior fibers blend into the supraspinous ligament.
bands.source: Bogduk N. Clinical and Radiological Anatomy of the Lumbar Spine, 5th ed. Churchill Livingstone/Elsevier, 2012 -- spinal ligament anatomy and biomechanical role.

function: Connects adjacent spinous processes; part of the posterior ligamentous complex resisting flexion, weaker than the supraspinous ligament it blends into posteriorly.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Bogduk N. Clinical and Radiological Anatomy of the Lumbar Spine, 5th ed. Churchill Livingstone/Elsevier, 2012 -- spinal ligament anatomy and biomechanical role.

bands.name: Supraspinous ligament

attachments.landmark_b: spinous process tips, continuing to the sacrum

bands.mechanical_role: resists spinal flexion; the most posterior (longest lever arm) of the posterior ligamentous complex, continuous superiorly with the ligamentum nuchae above C7
bands.function_note: Runs along the very tips of the spinous processes from C7 to the sacrum and is continuous above C7 with the ligamentum nuchae, which is modeled as a separate named entity here given its distinct cervical-specific anatomy.
bands.source: Bogduk N. Clinical and Radiological Anatomy of the Lumbar Spine, 5th ed. Churchill Livingstone/Elsevier, 2012 -- spinal ligament anatomy and biomechanical role.

function: The most posterior and mechanically most efficient (longest moment arm) element of the posterior ligamentous complex resisting flexion, from C7 to the sacrum.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Bogduk N. Clinical and Radiological Anatomy of the Lumbar Spine, 5th ed. Churchill Livingstone/Elsevier, 2012 -- spinal ligament anatomy and biomechanical role.

bands.name: Ligamentum nuchae

attachments.landmark_b: spinous processes C1(tubercle)-C7, in a triangular sheet

bands.mechanical_role: resists cervical flexion and provides an attachment septum between the paired posterior neck muscles; the cervical-region continuation of the supraspinous ligament
bands.function_note: A broad triangular fibroelastic septum (not a simple cord) that also serves as a muscle attachment site (trapezius, splenius capitis, rhomboid minor, serratus posterior superior all attach along it) -- functionally the cervical spine's counterpart to the thoracolumbar supraspinous ligament, and unusually elastic-fiber-rich in quadrupeds (where it helps passively support head weight), though less pronounced functionally in upright humans.
bands.source: Bogduk N. Clinical and Radiological Anatomy of the Lumbar Spine, 5th ed. Churchill Livingstone/Elsevier, 2012 -- spinal ligament anatomy and biomechanical role.

function: The cervical continuation of the supraspinous ligament; a fibroelastic median septum resisting flexion and providing a shared posterior-neck-muscle attachment site.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Bogduk N. Clinical and Radiological Anatomy of the Lumbar Spine, 5th ed. Churchill Livingstone/Elsevier, 2012 -- spinal ligament anatomy and biomechanical role.
